uncited: This family comprises methods to extract explicit triangular meshes from trained 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models.
Standard 3DGS represents scenes as implicit volumetric primitives, lacking a native surface representation.
These methods solve the problem of obtaining watertight, textured geometry for downstream applications like simulation, AR/VR, or editing.

They differ from sibling methods like [Radiative and Tomographic Gaussians](4971-radiative-and-tomographic-gaussians.md) by focusing on geometric extraction rather than physical property rendering, and from [Domain-Specific Adaptations](5621-domain-specific-adaptations.md) by targeting general mesh generation rather than specific domain constraints like microscopy.
All methods in this family operate on the output of a trained 3DGS model $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$.

Each primitive $G_i$ is defined by position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\mathbf{\Sigma}_i$, opacity $\alpha_i$, and color attributes [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).
The core challenge is converting these anisotropic, volumetric kernels into a discrete surface representation.

This requires either evaluating the implicit density field defined by the Gaussians, leveraging geometric cues (depth/normal) rendered from the splats, or modifying the splat distribution to align with an existing mesh.
The extraction of meshes from 3DGS is a necessary step for integrating neural radiance fields and Gaussian splats into traditional computer graphics pipelines.
Early 3DGS implementations focused solely on novel view synthesis [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).
Subsequent research identified the lack of explicit geometry as a limitation for applications requiring collision detection or texture mapping.

Methods like GOF [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md] and Poisson-based extraction [12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md] emerged to bridge this gap, while distance-based approaches [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md] addressed geometric consistency in large-scale scenes.
